data.narrative:
Electric Hydrogen, a Series C climate and energy company founded by Raffi Garabedian and David Eaglesham, is valued at $1.0B post-money following $700M in total capital raised. The valuation analysis benchmarks against a universe of nine comparable companies—one public (Lanza Tech, LNZA) and eight private peers in the same sector and stage, including KoBold Metals, Amogy, and Redwood Materials.

Two valuation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis, applying a typical 1.7x step-up multiplier from Series C to the next funding stage, implies a value of $1.7B. Peer-median analysis across three same-sector comparables—KoBold Metals ($3.0B, Series C), Amogy ($700M, Series C), and Redwood Materials ($6.0B, Series D)—yields a $3.0B median, establishing a range of $700M to $6.0B. The wide spread reflects heterogeneity in technology maturity and capital intensity across the climate tech peer set.

Triangulating these methods produces a valuation range of $1.4B (low) to $3.4B (high), with a median of $2.3B. This implies 40–240% upside from the current $1.0B valuation. Key uncertainties include the timeline to commercial-scale deployment, capital efficiency relative to peers, and technology validation risk inherent to frontier-stage climate hardware ventures. The peer-median method carries higher uncertainty given the small comparable sample and wide dispersion in stage and growth profile.
